purpose: Records the relock of the OpenHands recipe lock (blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/requirements.lock) from litellm 1.93.0 to 1.93.2. OSV published GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222 (CVE-2026-84377, 'LiteLLM: Authenticated SSRF and provider-credential exfiltration via unvalidated request-body routing parameters', GitHub severity Moderate, CVSS 3.1 6.5, CWE-918) at 2026-09-30T21:11:25Z for litellm 1.93.0 and 1.93.1; 1.93.2 is the first release of the 1.93 line without it. The scan workflow concluded failure in every run that section J lists between the record's publication and this pull request's own run (pull-request heads and main's own push runs); the one job log read (run 36786110610) shows the required osv-scanner job failing on exactly this finding. A required check that fails on main's own lock keeps every pull request from merging. The change replaces the litellm requirement line and its hashes and nothing else in the lock, rebinds the lock's IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry in tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py to the relocked sha256 and to this record (the 2026-09-29 oauthlib review is carried forward at the new digest, not rerun), and adds no ignore.
authorization: The lock's previous owner (a peer session of the Claude lane, named on #518) is gone: a peer listing on 2026-09-30 no longer shows it. The merge-train owner asked the Gate A owner (the session that wrote this record) to take the relock and to relock rather than ignore. Peer messages are not retained evidence; the reproductions in sections B, D and F of the returned outputs are. No user decision is needed: the change extends the recipe's own method (research.md 'Runtime lock security relock') by one upgrade and a two-line edit of the extracted workspace, and adds no exception.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's config and the workflow's own lockfile lists, a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv on the host network (no model request: not the image and not an OpenHands run), reads of registry and advisory records (OSV API, PyPI JSON API), blobless depth-1 fetches of two upstream git tags (BerriAI/litellm v1.93.0 and v1.93.2) and of upstream SDK main (section C), reads of the GitHub API for the scan workflow's runs and one job log (section J), a fetch and dry-run merges of three open pull requests' heads (section K), and two independent reviews (independent_review). Static and local: the diffs, hash equalities, syntax-tree and text searches are structural checks, not executions. Returned outputs: blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/evidence/relock-2026-09-30-litellm.txt.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock, which still pins litellm 1.93.0 (section C: the archive's root uv.lock, line 2175), and the 2026-09-28 grype record of that image predates the OSV record's publication (2026-09-30T21:11:25Z; the advisory's NVD record, 2026-09-02, is older). A rerun would not measure it either: that record says 'The PyInstaller single-file server archive is not unpacked by the catalogers, so this scan neither confirms nor excludes the four upstream-lock versions' (python_package_matches 0). Whether the advisory reaches the image's binary is unmeasured. The grader venv (OpenHands/benchmarks@405bae7's uv.lock, digest in pins.json grader.uv_lock_sha256) is outside this lock and outside .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json; its litellm version was not read.

The advisory concerns the LiteLLM proxy: an authenticated proxy user routing a provider call with request-body parameters the proxy did not validate. The recipe runs no LiteLLM proxy, and no installed package outside litellm references litellm.proxy (section H: a search by syntax tree of the installed .py files of the relocked venv: 8877 parsed, 1 not parsed (func_timeout/py2_raise.py, SyntaxError), 28 of them import litellm or a submodule, 0 references to litellm.proxy; it finds imports, from-imports in any form, attribute access and string constants that name litellm.proxy). That is a static search, not a runtime trace; a name assembled at run time would not match. It is context only: the change moves to the fixed release and the decision does not rest on reachability.

No OpenHands task ran with the relocked venv. The install check ran the recipe's install sequence, uv pip check and the SDK import check on the host network (no model request); the image installation, model behavior and any runtime path through litellm 1.93.2 are unmeasured. An installation that recorded the old requirements_sha256 must re-run install (host.py:1432-1433 refuses with matching_successful_installation_required); whether this host holds such a record was not checked for this change.

litellm 1.93.2 differs from 1.93.0 in 34 files of upstream source (section C): proxy auth, health, SSO and server modules, two library files outside the proxy (litellm/caching/dual_cache.py: the in-memory TTL of a value read back from Redis; litellm/litellm_core_utils/url_utils.py: one new helper function), two provider modules (huggingface embedding, oobabooga), the non-root Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, uv.lock and tests. None is under the paths the recipe cites or calls (litellm/llms/openai, litellm/responses, litellm/main.py, litellm/router.py, litellm/types, litellm/utils.py). The comparison is of upstream source at the two tags; the installed wheels were verified against the lock's hashes only and were not diffed against those tags.

The upstream workspace cannot produce this lock as published: its pyproject.toml pins litellm==1.93.0 (line 19) and caps litellm at exclude-newer-package 2026-07-20T00:00:00Z (line 8), which excludes 1.93.1 and 1.93.2. The relock edits both lines in a scratch extraction (section B prints the whole diff); the upstream lock, the agent-server image and the SDK's own release are unchanged. The next upstream lock that carries litellm >= 1.93.2 makes the edit unnecessary.

The OSV database is the live API at scan time. The clean result holds for 2026-09-30 only: an advisory published later for any pinned package fails the required check again. Every statement about a release window is as of 2026-09-30T23:47:02Z: litellm 1.93.2's files were uploaded 2026-08-09T02:16:21Z to 02:17:49Z, 52 days earlier.

The ignore reasons of the two oauthlib advisories in .github/osv-scanner.toml still cite evidence/receipts/osv-openhands-pyjwt-relock-20260930.json for the OpenHands lock 'at its relocked sha256'; that text already lagged the 2026-09-30 urllib3 relock and is unchanged here (PR #535 edits the same file). The binding record is the IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry of tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py, which this change rebinds. The dated paragraph that each earlier relock added to docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md is also not added here: PR #555 edits that file, so the paragraph follows its merge.

Three open pull requests change files this change touches (section K, heads fetched at 2026-09-30T23:46:41Z): #535 (head ff79d96a) replaces this lock and pins.json with a candidate built from SDK archive dcf401af (litellm==1.93.2, oauthlib 3.3.1, pyjwt 2.15.0, urllib3 2.8.0 at that head; requirements_sha256 38c20c89...) and conflicts with this change in pins.json, requirements.lock, manifests/evidence.json and tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py (dry-run merge); #551 (head 0e86cb7e) and #555 (head 8c263ace) conflict with it only in manifests/evidence.json, and tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py merges without conflict in both. The owner of #535 has to rebase it onto this change's merge and keep its own lock and digest in the IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry; this change does not depend on it.

Two edits are deferred to the pull requests that change the same files, and have an owner: the dated paragraph of docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md (#555 edits that file), and the ignore reasons in .github/osv-scanner.toml, which still name the previous owner session and cite the PyJWT receipt for the OpenHands lock (#535 edits that file). Owner of both: the Gate A owner session (this record's author), after #555 and #535 merge and before the 2026-10-13 expiry of the two oauthlib ignores; if either has not merged by 2026-10-09 the edits go in a change of their own. After 2026-10-13 the OpenHands lock fails the required check unless the #518 relock, or #535's candidate lock with its own IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry, has landed.
